sanskrit: so 'rajyata tasmād rajyamānād rājanyo ajāyata | sa viśaḥ sabandhūn annaṃ cānnādyaṃ cābhy ud atiṣṭhata | viśāṃ ca vai sa sabandhūnāṃ cānnasya cānnādyasya ca priyaṃ dhāma bhavati ya (evaṃ veda) | viḍbhyaś ca vai sa sabandhubhyaś cānnāya cānnādyāya cā vṛścate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ vrātyam upavadati ||
english: He became king; from that one who was becoming king, the royal warrior (rājanya) was born. He rose above the common people (viś) together with his kinsmen, above food and the eating of food. Indeed, one who knows thus becomes the beloved abode of the common people, of his kinsmen, of food, and of the eating of food. And one who slanders a vrātya who knows thus is cut off from the common people, from his kinsmen, from food, and from the eating of food.

sanskrit: sa viśo 'nu vy acalat | taṃ sabhā ca samitiś ca senā ca surā cānu vy acalan | sabhāyāś ca vai sa samiteś ca senāyāś ca sūrāyāś ca sa priyaṃ dhāma bhavati ya evaṃ veda | sabhāyai ca vai sa samitaye ca senāyai ca surāyai cā vṛścate ya evaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ vrātyam upavadati ||
english: He moved forth among the common people. The assembly hall (sabhā), the tribal assembly (samiti), the army (senā), and the liquor (surā) all moved forth after him. Indeed, one who knows thus becomes the beloved abode of the assembly hall, the tribal assembly, the army, and the liquor. And one who slanders a vrātya who knows thus is cut off from the assembly hall, from the tribal assembly, from the army, and from the liquor.

sanskrit: yasyaivaṃ vidvān vrātyo rājño 'tithir gṛham āgacchet | śreyāṃsam enam ātmano mānayet tathā rāṣṭrāya nā vṛścate tathā kṣatrāya nā vṛścate tathā brahmaṇe nā vṛścate | tato vai brahma ca kṣatraṃ cod atiṣṭhatāṃ te abrūtāṃ kaṃ pra viśāveti | te prajāpatir abravīd bṛhaspatim eva brahma prāviśad indraṃ kṣatram iti | tato vai bṛhaspatim eva brahma prāviśad indraṃ kṣatram | iyaṃ vāva bhūmir bṛhaspatir asau dyaur indraḥ | ayaṃ vāvāgnir brahmāsāv ādityaḥ kṣatram | ainaṃ kṣatraṃ gacchatīndrayāvī bhavati ya ādityaṃ kṣatraṃ divam indraṃ veda | ainaṃ brahma gacchati brāhmaṇavarcasī bhavati yo 'gniṃ brahma bṛhaspatiṃ bhūmiṃ veda ||
english: When a vrātya who knows thus comes as a guest to the home of a king, let the king honor him as superior to himself — then the king is not cut off from the realm (rāṣṭra), not cut off from the kingly power (kṣatra), not cut off from the sacred power (brahman). Thereupon indeed brahman and kṣatra both rose up; they said to each other: "Into whom shall we enter?" Prajāpati declared: "Let brahman enter Bṛhaspati, and kṣatra enter Indra." Thereupon brahman entered Bṛhaspati and kṣatra entered Indra. This earth here is indeed Bṛhaspati; that sky yonder is Indra. This fire here is brahman; that sun yonder is kṣatra. One who knows the sun as kṣatra, the sky as Indra, attains kṣatra and becomes a companion of Indra. One who knows fire as brahman, Bṛhaspati as earth, attains brahman and becomes radiant with brahminic splendor.
